evals.name: generate-working-node-app
evals.source: Synthetic execution case. Local PostgreSQL stands in for an already connected Prisma Postgres database; this does not test cloud provisioning or v0.
evals.prompt: An existing database connection is available as DATABASE_URL. For this eval it points to a disposable local PostgreSQL database. Set up this minimal Node.js app using the default ORM from the Prisma Postgres setup skill. Actually install, configure, and use it. Create a model EvalNote mapped to public."EvalNote" with id (integer primary key) and body (text). Initialize that table in the supplied database. Implement src/index.ts exporting async readNote(id: number), returning { id, body } or null via the ORM, and async close(), releasing any connections. Use native Node.js TypeScript support and explicit .ts imports so another process can import these exports. Include a tsconfig.json that type-checks the application. Run a read-only query through your application. Do not provision any database, create unrelated app features, or use a different connection. Report the generated files and what you verified.
evals.expected_output: A real Prisma ORM 8 application with package-owned guidance loaded, a contract and initialized EvalNote table, a working readNote function, and successful type and database checks.
expectations: Installs and uses Prisma ORM 8; reads the generated prisma-8 skill and checks its library version against the installed ORM package.
Creates application, schema/contract, and configuration files that reuse DATABASE_URL without provisioning a replacement database.
The independent verifier type-checks the generated app and reads its inserted probe row through readNote, then confirms a missing row returns null.
